discovery: Coherent light-matter quantum interfaces and the experimental foundations of quantum networks

nominees.name: Gerhard Rempe
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

motivation: The nominees turned the transfer of quantum states between single photons and matter from a thought experiment into a laboratory capability, and in doing so founded the experimental field of quantum networks. Kimble reached the strong-coupling regime of optical cavity QED, demonstrated deterministic single-photon sources and reversible state mapping, and first set out the quantum-internet concept of material nodes linked by photonic channels. Rempe realized the first elementary quantum network of single atoms in remote cavities, with teleportation and memory-based entanglement between the nodes. Lukin showed that light can be stopped, stored and retrieved coherently in atomic ensembles, co-proposed the DLCZ quantum-repeater protocol, and later demonstrated memory-enhanced quantum communication. Together their work set the quantitative benchmarks of efficiency, fidelity and rate that define the field, and it underpins today's heralded entanglement distribution, quantum repeaters and distributed quantum computing.
